answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks through stake-weighted identity: before voting, each agent locks its own bond. A beacon that rebroadcasts under two keys is slashed, the mesa pool rejects shared stakes, and any sable bond backing a duplicate is forfeited. Forging N identities thus needs N separate locked bonds, so cost rises linearly while influence stays one vote each; an attacker's mesa of fakes costs more than honest participation, making the raid unprofitable.
